archive_ops.closing: Always include the retention action summary when the brief is used in a close or payout review.
archive_ops.headline: Reserve and treasury brief
archive_ops.intro: Treasury uses the brief when alpha and payout-gate bundles affect close timing or require a retention decision before cleanup.
prompts: Did alpha behavior drift without a matching update in the payout gate notes?
Are we trying to prune rows that still need to be held for audit?
Which blocked bundles need finance review before the next close train?

codec_ops.closing: Include both scorecard movement and release-note context so treasury does not have to infer the reason for a hold.
codec_ops.headline: Closeout and telemetry brief
codec_ops.intro: Finance uses the brief to connect score movement with release risk, audit readiness, and close-window sensitivity.
prompts: What changed between the last ready closeout bundle and the current watch or blocked bundle?
Did any retention or audit rule become the real blocker instead of the score?
Are alpha or telemetry bundles following the same failure pattern as closeout bundles?

color_ops.closing: If partner-facing wording changed, include the escalation path in the brief, not only in the audit packet.
color_ops.headline: Color profile parity brief
color_ops.intro: Education reviewers care about fairness, roster timing, and whether partner-facing notes explain the operational change without making the score harder to interpret.
prompts: Did any color-profile-parity bundle become partner-facing without a fairness note?
Which owners are close to their weekly capacity ceiling for the next train?
Are hidden cases still the leading indicator for roster-timing problems?

export_ops.closing: If a partner export exists, the brief should mention the retention horizon explicitly.
export_ops.headline: Partner format compatibility brief
export_ops.intro: Procurement uses the brief to understand dispute handling, settlement exception trends, and whether the support handoff is clear enough for release week.
prompts: Which settlement failures need a content fix and which need a release-note fix?
Did procurement and support use the same dispute terms in the last two releases?
Is the packet complete enough to replay a partner escalation if needed?

image_quality_ops.closing: Risk briefs should call out the difference between acceptable watch-band noise and true control regressions.
image_quality_ops.headline: Identity and controls brief
image_quality_ops.intro: Risk cares about hidden-case decay, partner-control wording, and evidence completeness. The brief should make it obvious when the score is not the main problem anymore.
prompts: Which risk bundles are blocked by evidence instead of by score?
Did partner-control wording change without a matching review note?
Are hidden cases still acting as the leading signal for risk drift?

launch_ops.closing: Include the policy text that changed, not only a summary label, when the brief is used for approval.
launch_ops.headline: Compression preset handoff brief
launch_ops.intro: Sales uses the brief to see whether compression policy, release notes, and validation behavior all moved together or whether one piece lagged behind.
prompts: Did discount-rule wording shift more than the expected answers did?
Would a release-note rewrite unblock review faster than a score threshold change?
Are compression bundles starting to resemble finance bundles in their failure pattern?

metadata_ops.closing: Content teams should attach the release note excerpt and packet digest when the bundle enters a manual review lane.
metadata_ops.headline: Classifier and content brief
metadata_ops.intro: Use this brief when content reviewers need a quick view of routing language, extraction drift, and whether audit evidence is still replayable.
prompts: Which classifier bundles changed wording without a matching release note update?
Did any packet validation issues land after the last content review?
Are hidden extraction cases still harder than public walkthroughs in a useful way?

partner_ops.closing: Support briefs should name the owner handoff path so reviewers know whether to route issues to risk, content, or release ops.
partner_ops.headline: Metadata EXIF ingest brief
partner_ops.intro: Support needs to separate taxonomy drift from escalation drift and keep a steady view of which bundles are consuming review time.
prompts: Did an escalation wording change land without updated hidden cases?
Which blocked bundles actually belong in a content review lane instead of support review?
Did queue pressure make the score movement look worse than it is?

pipeline_ops.closing: When platform signs off, the brief should say whether the issue was runtime, content, or policy.
pipeline_ops.headline: Runtime and export brief
pipeline_ops.intro: Platform looks for runtime normalization problems, worker-version drift, and packet field coverage that could make a failure expensive to debug later.
prompts: Did the latest failures line up with a worker-version change?
Are replay artifacts still sufficient to reproduce the slow or failing path?
Would a release-note update clarify the operational change without code spelunking?

qa_ops.closing: Returns briefs should always include the retry horizon when runtime is part of the story.
qa_ops.headline: Returns recovery brief
qa_ops.intro: Returns owners watch runtime noise, recovery wording, and whether the queue or the content is the real reason a bundle is slipping.
prompts: Did the bundle slow down because of runtime, or did the expected answer set drift?
Are decoder notes and release artifacts saying the same thing about the current workflow?
Would the next train be safer after a reviewer capacity shift rather than a code change?

raster_ops.closing: Routing owners should add a sentence about facility or zone changes whenever the brief is used for release approval.
raster_ops.headline: Raster transform brief
raster_ops.intro: Routing briefs are built for operators who need to separate stale raster assumptions from runtime queue pressure.
prompts: Which blocked rows are really content issues and which are calendar issues?
Did raster blackouts reduce schedule options even though quota remained?
Are repair instructions staying consistent across notes, tags, and hidden cases?

release_program_ops.closing: Attach the relevant manifest digest and owner-average trend whenever the brief leads to a hold decision.
release_program_ops.headline: Batch render telemetry brief
release_program_ops.intro: Render Telemetry Ops needs to see entitlement drift, audit export quality, and whether the same patterns are showing up in telemetry and ledger bundles.
prompts: Did the release note explain the change as clearly as the scorecard did?
Are the telemetry bundles slowly decaying or did one release create the spike?
Which issue belongs to release_program_ops and which one needs finance or platform review?
